Technical summary: using hosted_api streaming with function/tool calling. They register function manifest where params have snake_case keys, but client code expects camelCase. When model emits function call, param names mismatch -> schema validation fails in their runtime (pydantic schema).

Observed failure modes: 1) streaming chunk boundary splits JSON object causing temporary parse error when client tries to parse partial buffer; 2) model-produced function_call arguments sometimes use hyphenated keys; 3) when json_mode=true, model sometimes wraps payload in extra metadata field 'output' which breaks strict schema expectations.

What we've recommended: 1) set streaming debug flag to include chunk indices and boundary markers; 2) use buffering at client to wait for complete top-level JSON before parse; 3) use a permissive intermediate schema that tolerates camel/snake variants and normalizes keys server-side; 4) enable function_call strict mode in runtime so model uses exact schema names.
